# #265 — Sprint: gbrain-informed graph retrieval and operator hardening

## Sprint intent

Turn the useful parts of the gbrain audit into scoped Open Brain enhancements without importing gbrain wholesale.

## Why

The audit found that Open Brain already has the right graph substrate (`ob_entities`, `ob_links`, `adjacent_context`), but graph links do not currently participate in search ranking. gbrain's strongest pattern is retrieval-time typed-edge recall: parse relational questions, resolve seed entities, traverse typed links, hydrate linked evidence into normal search rows, and prove the change with an A/B no-regression eval.

## Sprint pairs

Pair A - graph retrieval and proof:

- #266 - Add relational retrieval eval/no-regression fixtures.
- #267 - Add a graph-powered relational retrieval arm to `search_brain`.
- Rule: the retrieval arm must not land without the eval gate that proves relational lift and normal-query no-regression.

Pair B - answer/context consumption:

- #268 - Expose graph-expanded evidence safely in `brain_answer` / `search_all`.
- #271 - Evaluate a lightweight hot-memory/context-pack injection path after the retrieval arm exists.

Pair C - operator hardening:

- #269 - Add privacy-safe MCP/tool request audit logging.
- #270 - Add an operator `doctor/status` surface for Open Brain health.

## Non-goals

- No new graph database.
- No visual graph UI in this sprint.
- No gbrain schema import.
- No public behavior change without namespace/auth regression tests.
- No NATS/fleet-bus scope; issue #223 owns transport.

## Done when

- Each child issue has acceptance criteria, validation expectations, and downstream impact classification.
- Project #8 tracks each issue with priority/component/surface/phase/review/validation fields.
- Pair A is treated as the first sprint gate.
